text: The "normal readings" for gestational age seem inconsistent with the classic presentation of Respiratory Distress Syndrome, which typically affects premature infants. speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity (born at 32 weeks), consistent with ground-glass opacities on X-ray despite normal blood culture and CBC. The cesarean section may have contributed to retained fetal lung fluid, but the prematurity and specific radiographic findings strongly point to RDS.
